claim: Let \(G\) be a finite connected simple graph on \(n\ge 5\) vertices and \(e\) edges. Assume that \(G\) is triangle-free, has no \(4\)-cycle, and has diameter at most \(2\). Then the ordinary cut complexes satisfy the simplicial collapse \(\Delta_2(G)\searrow\Delta_3(G)\). Consequently \(\Delta_3(G)\simeq\bigvee^{e-n+1}S^{n-4}\), with a zero-fold wedge interpreted as contractible. In particular, for the Petersen graph \(P\), \(\Delta_3(P)\simeq\bigvee^{6}S^6\).
integrity: The family theorem is proved directly by explicit free codimension-one faces. The published 2-cut homotopy theorem is used only after that collapse. The Petersen calculation is independently reconstructed by exhaustive face enumeration and an acyclic discrete-Morse matching.
scientific_limitations: The collapse uses triangle-freeness, absence of 4-cycles, and diameter at most 2; it does not classify 3-cut complexes outside this class or assert shellability. The finite computation is a sanity check rather than the proof of the family theorem.
title: A collapse from 2-cut to 3-cut complexes in unique-common-neighbor graphs
